questions.question: A patient is intended to be treated with 12 implanted Pd-103 seeds with an activity at implant of 0.42 mCi/seed. The seeds are ordered from a vendor and arrive 3 days before implant. On the day the seeds arrive, what is batch activity should be measured during a survey?
questions.solution: Decay-correct to the assay day: 0.42 mCi/seed x 12 × 2^(3/17) = 5.69 mCi.

questions.question: Cesium-137 is sometimes used as a substitute for Radium-226 in Brachytherapy. What properties make it a good substitute? (Select all that apply)
options: There is no gas build up in a sealed Cs-137 source
Cs-137 has a lower exposure rate constant allowing for smaller source sizes.
Cs-137 has a similar average photon energy to Ra-226
questions.answer: Cs-137 emits only photons; there is no gas buildup in a sealed Cs-137 source; Cs-137 has a similar average photon energy to Ra-226
questions.solution: Cs-137 avoids radon gas buildup and has a photon spectrum closer to radium than many alternatives.

questions.question: Which of the following statements are true regarding radioactive sources? (select all that apply)
options: Transient equilibrium occurs when the half life of a daughter is much greater than the parent.
Secular equilibrium occurs when the half life of a daughter is much greater
Half life is inversely proportional to the decay constant.
radium needle used in brachytherapy is under the condition of secular equilibrium.
questions.answer: Half-life is inversely proportional to the decay constant; a radium needle is in secular equilibrium
questions.solution: T1/2 = ln2/lambda. Ra-226 daughters are short-lived compared with the parent, giving secular equilibrium after sealing.

questions.question: Why is quenching an MRI scanner dangerous?
options: Quenching rapidly stops all moving components of the scanner which results in significant wear.
Rapidly heating the superconducting primary coils will damage them.
Ferromagnetic objects placed too near the magnetic field can be propelled with great force into the scanner.
Rapidly fluctuating magnetic fields have been known to cause severe burns

questions.solution: A quench rapidly transitions superconducting coils to a resistive state and can be hazardous to the scanner; helium boil-off is also a major real-world safety issue.

questions.question: How to Klystrons amplify microwave energy?
options: Input microwave energy interacts with a perpendicular magnetic field causing electrons to process in a characteristic microwave frequency.
Input microwave energy differentially accelerates electrons. After a brief drifting period, amplified energy is removed from electron bunches.
Input microwave energy is amplified by resonance withing the drift tube and finally removed from bunched electrons.
Input microwave energy is used to accelerate electrons from cathode to anode.
Higher energy microwaves are created when the electrons reach the anode.
questions.answer: Input microwave energy differentially accelerates electrons; after drift, amplified energy is removed from electron bunches.
questions.solution: A klystron velocity-modulates electrons, bunches them in a drift region, and extracts amplified RF power from the bunched beam.

Higher energy electrons deposit energy more uniformly along their path than low energy electrons.
Higher energy electrons are less likely to scatter at large angles.
Higher energy electron beams have more lateral expansion at the low isodose levels than lower energy beams.
questions.answer: Higher energy electrons are less likely to scatter at large angles.
questions.solution: Higher-energy electrons scatter more forward, so more electrons reach shallow depths and surface dose increases.

questions.question: A two arc plan is prepared to deliver 70 Gy in 33 fractions. The machine is calibrated to 1.00 cGy/MU. How many MU are required for arc 1? Arc 1: Relative weight = 1 Angle TMR 30 0.714 50 0.730 70 0.733 90 0.720 110 0.710 Arc 2: Relative weight = 0.5 Angle TMR 210 0.617 230 0.593 250 0.601 270 0.605 290 0.614
questions.solution: Dose per fraction = 70 Gy/33 = 212 cGy. Arc 1 gets 1/(1+0.5) of the dose. Using the mean arc-1 TMR about 0.721, MU = 141 cGy/0.721 = 196 MU.
